voltinism variability is higher in the Mediterranean than in Scandinavia and that the Tachet database is not able to represent voltinism variability in the Mediterranean or Scandinavian regions.

(i) the Tachet database is a reliable source of voltinism information across Europe, (ii) voltinism is a labile life history trait, and (iii) intra taxon variability should be taken into account when using trait databases.

1) the Tachet Trait database (TAC) provides an adequate representation of voltinism variability in Europe, 2) voltinism variability is not well captured by the TAC database when applied to the Mediterranean Basin and 3) voltinism in the Mediterranean Basin is more complex than previously assumed.

the role of intra-taxon trait variability in community ecology, and how it affects the use of trait databases in ecology.
the reliability of trait databases in studies that use them for large regions with contrasting environments.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of trait databases should be carefully considered, and the use of these databases in studies that aim at understanding trait-environment relationships in large areas should be done with caution, especially for labile traits.
voltinism is a labile taxonomically constrained trait that is not properly represented in current trait databases, especially in the Mediterranean Basin.

the Tachet database provides a good representation for the voltinism variability in Europe, and that the use of the database for the Mediterranean region or the Scandinavian region would require a better representation of the univoltine or multivoltine taxa, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that

trait databases should be used carefully, especially when they are used to test hypotheses about trait environment relationships across large regions or in particular regions with particular environmental characteristics.
the use of a trait database for labile traits in a particular region may be problematic if it does not accurately represent trait variability across the region.
